title: TM Synchronization and Channel Coding
issue: Recommended Standard, Issue 6 (Blue Book), with Editorial Correction 1 (May 2026)
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) lists issues B-1 (September 2003), B-2 (August 2011), B-3 (September 2017), B-4 (April 2022) and B-5 (September 2023) as superseded. 131.0-B-6 (April 2026) is the 'Current issue': it adds an interleaver for Turbo codewords, allows slicing with all block codes (so Transfer Frame lengths need not match the code) and makes the pseudo-randomizer mandatory. Editorial Correction 1 (May 2026) fixes numbering in the table of contents, table C-1 and figures 3-1, 3-2, 3-3 and F-1. Substantive changes are marked with change bars.

key_points.text: Issue 6 (April 2026) replaces issue 5 (September 2023): it adds a channel interleaver for Turbo codewords, allows slicing with all block codes and makes the pseudo-randomizer mandatory; Editorial Correction 1 is dated May 2026.
The sublayer provides four functions: error-control coding including frame validation, Transfer Frame slicing, synchronization, and pseudo-randomizing.
Transfer Frame slicing is optional with R-S, Turbo or LDPC coding, fixed for a mission phase, and must not be used with uncoded data or convolutional coding alone.

With slicing, each M-bit Transfer Frame is prefixed with the 32-bit ASM 0x1ACFFC1D to form an SMTF; the SMTF stream is cut into k-bit Information Blocks, encoded, randomized (mandatory) and given CSMs. The ASM cannot be confused with the identical 32-bit CSM because the ASM is randomized.
Without slicing each Transfer Frame is one Information Block, there is a single level of synchronization, and the terms CSM and ASM are interchangeable.

With no coding, convolutional coding or Turbo coding the FECF is mandatory for frame validation; with R-S, concatenated or LDPC coding the decoder may validate, and with slicing a frame is invalid if any part of it lies in an invalid Information Block.

Basic convolutional code: non-systematic, r = 1/2, K = 7, G1 = 1111001 (171 octal), G2 = 1011011 (133 octal), with symbol inversion on the G2 output path; puncturing gives one of the rates 2/3, 3/4, 5/6 or 7/8.
Reed-Solomon: E = 16 gives the (255,223) code and E = 8 the (255,239) code; allowable interleaving depths are I = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8.

Turbo channel interleaver (7.3.12): a row-column interleaver of depth 4 with Nc = 4/r = 8, 12, 16 or 24 columns, external to the Turbo encoder's own bit permutation; its use is a managed parameter and it is highly recommended for tumbling spacecraft or solar scintillation.
The CADU is the CSM plus the randomized Transfer Frame, R-S codeblock, Turbo codeword or LDPC codeword, formed before any convolutional encoding.

CSM patterns: 0x1ACFFC1D (uncoded, convolutional, R-S, concatenated, rate-7/8 LDPC); 0x034776C7272895B0 (rate-1/2 Turbo and rate-1/2, 2/3, 4/5 LDPC); 96-, 128- and 192-bit markers for rate-1/3, 1/4 and 1/6 Turbo.
The CSM is never presented to the R-S, Turbo or LDPC encoder or decoder; it is attached directly to the codeword or codeblock.
The CSM synchronizes the pseudo-randomizer; the sequence starts at the first bit after the CSM, and the CSM itself is not randomized.
The pseudo-randomizer is mandatory for all combinations of CCSDS modulation and coding; the note records telemetry link problems on missions that did not use it.

The pseudo-random sequence is 131071 bits long, h(x) = x^17 + x^14 + 1, seeded with '11000111000111000'; the legacy 255-bit sequence h(x) = x^8 + x^7 + x^5 + x^3 + 1 (all-ones seed) may be used for backward compatibility but may cause spectral lines at 1/255 of the symbol rate.

No frame-length constraint applies when slicing is used, when data are uncoded or with convolutional coding alone (maximum 2048 octets for TM, 65536 for AOS and USLP); without slicing R-S frames are L = (255-2E-q)I octets, Turbo frames 223, 446, 892 or 1115 octets, rate-7/8 LDPC frames 892 octets and rate-1/2, 2/3, 4/5 LDPC frames 128, 512 or 2048 octets.

Managed parameters now include Randomizer (Long 131071 bits or Short 255 bits), Slicing (Present/Absent) for R-S, Turbo and LDPC, and Channel Interleaver (Present/Absent) for Turbo; all are fixed on a Physical Channel for a Mission Phase.
Turbo codes suit power-constrained links beyond low-Earth orbit; LDPC codes suit high-data-rate, bandwidth-limited links; either may be selected for AOS or USLP ground-to-space links.
The service (Annex A) is ChannelAccess.request(Frame) and ChannelAccess.indication(Frame, Quality Indicator, Sequence Indicator); only one user may use the service on a Physical Channel.

notes: Newer issue of the library item ccsds-131-0-131x0b5 (Issue 5, September 2023), which it supersedes; the section numbering differs (B-5 sections 3 to 8 become 4 to 8 after the new slicing section 3, B-5's separate section on LDPC coding of a stream of SMTFs is folded into the general slicing scheme, and B-5's 'Frame Synchronization' becomes 'Codeword Synchronization'; the B-5 embedded-data-stream ASM 0x352EF853 no longer appears). PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate covers; the extraction has 100 PDF pages (registry: 99). Inconsistencies as printed: the Document Control row for Issue 5 is labelled 'CCSDS 131.0-B-6'; reference [6] gives 'Issue 3' with document number 732.1-B-2 and date October 2021; [E7] is cited as 'CCSDS 131.1-G-3' although the TM coding rationale Green Book is 130.1-G-3 (library item ccsds-130-1-130x1g3e1); the Annex E note says normative references are in 1.6 (they are in 1.7); the table of contents calls Annex C an annex to 7.3 while its heading says 8.3; Annex F refers to 'figure 13-1' (the figure is F-1); 10.2.5 says derandomization of Turbo/LDPC codewords happens 'after decoding', while 3.3.2 and 3.4.2 derandomize before decoding. Figure 7-5 and Table 7-4 are missing from the lists of figures and tables. The patent contact names, addresses, telephone numbers and e-mail addresses in Annex B3 are deliberately not reproduced. No individual authors are named.
